title: Tavi, the Slave of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a great Torah scholar, as stated explicitly in Mishnah Sukkah, beginning of chapter 2: “Rabbi Shimon said: An incident with Tavi, the slave of Rabban Gamliel, who was sleeping under the bed (in the sukkah). Rabban Gamliel said to the elders: Have you seen Tavi my slave, who is a Torah scholar and knows that slaves are exempt from the sukkah, and therefore sleeps under the bed?” (In the journal Ohel Yitzchak, issue 6, [5]666, section 8, a certain scholar [אחד דבי] asked: if he knows a simple law that slaves are exempt from the sukkah, shall he be called a Torah scholar? Hyman answered him in issue 7 that the proof that he was a Torah scholar is that he slept under the bed, and thereby he showed the students the law that one obligated in sukkah who sleeps under the bed has not fulfilled his obligation; this is a new law, not stated explicitly, and they learned it only from him.)

He was so dear to Rabban Gamliel that he let him wear tefillin, as in the Mekhilta, Bo, chapter 17. (And why he was not freed by putting on tefillin — because his master must put tefillin on him, as stated explicitly in Gittin 40a, and so it is ruled in the Rambam, Hilkhot Avadim 8:17; but here Rabban Gamliel permitted him to put on tefillin, and no more.) And what we find in Mishnah Pesachim 7:2, “Rabbi Tzadok said: An incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said to Tavi his slave: Go out and roast the Passover offering for me” — Hyman explains in the entry Rabban Gamliel that this is Rabban Gamliel the Elder, as they said in the Jerusalem Talmud, 1:4 [tractate unspecified here], that the house of Rabban Gamliel used to call their slaves “Abba Tavi” and their maidservants “Imma Tavta”; and as we find in Vayikra Rabbah 19:4, Rabban Gamliel also had a maidservant named Tavita.

Hyman describes Rabban Gamliel as always distressed because he wished to free him. It happened once that he blinded the eye of Tavi his slave, and he rejoiced greatly; he found Rabbi Yehoshua and told him the incident. But to his heart’s sorrow, Rabbi Yehoshua answered him that he could not set him free, because he had no witnesses, and Rabban Gamliel had confessed to a fine and was exempt, as in Bava Kamma 74b.

He is mentioned in Yoma 87a with great praise, where they said: “Canaan had many children who were fit to be ordained, like Tavi, the slave of Rabban Gamliel.” In Midrash Mishlei 9:21: an incident with Rabban Gamliel, with whom the elders were reclining, and Tavi his slave was standing and serving them. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah said: “Woe to you, Canaan, who have brought liability upon your sons … By right, Tavi should be reclining and I serving him.” Hyman draws attention to the great worth of Tavi in the sages’ eyes.
When Tavi died, Rabban Gamliel accepted condolences over him, although one does not accept condolences over slaves, and he said: “Tavi my slave was upright,” as in Berakhot 16b.

notes.text: The journal discussion is Hyman’s own reported exchange; תרסו is retained as the supplied year, with the draft’s inferred[5]666 disclosed. Returned Buber MidrashMishlei9 supports Canaan bringing liability on his SONS, not being obligated to invented masters; ברין is read בדין and לבינך as לבניך. לשבת is read לשבח with GREAT praise. The tefillin/freeing distinction, Elder-versus-YavnehGamliel distinction and repeated Tavi/Tavita names remain Hyman’s claims.

The consulted Mishnah Sukkah 2:1 explicitly includes Tavi sleeping under the bed and the lesson drawn from it. Gittin 40a and the consulted Rambam Avadim 8:17 distinguish the master placing tefillin on the slave from the slave wearing them without objection; Hyman’s permission account remains alongside this distinction. The exact Mekhilta and journal exchange remain Hyman-reported. The complete Buber Midrash Mishlei 9 supports Canaan bringing liability on his sons. Great praise, the Elder/Yavneh distinction, repeated Tavi/Tavita names and the witnessed-fine issue remain intact.
